### Observed differences

- The execution order of two activity groups reversed. In the earlier window the group A19, A23, A26, A27, A28 — present in about 17–24 in 100 traces — sat early in the case (mean relative position about 0.33), while A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 — present in every trace — sat late (about 0.62). In the later window the always-present group sat early (about 0.39–0.40) and the rarer group sat late (about 0.67–0.71). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010]
- Pairwise order relations flipped with them. A29 preceded each of A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 in about 98–99 in 100 traces in the earlier window; in the later window each of them preceded A29 in about 99 in 100. The reversal against A33 is equally complete (A33 first in about 99–100 in 100 earlier; the group first in about 96–97 in 100 later). Pairs between the two groups reversed as well: for example, A19 came before A20 in about 22 in 100 traces earlier and after it in about 16 in 100 later, and A23 before A24 (about 23 in 100) became A24 before A23 (about 22 in 100). [REL001, REL003, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL016, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL029, REL030, REL035]
- Outgoing transitions moved with the positions. Earlier, A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 led almost exclusively to A29 (about 91–100 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions); in the later window they lead to A34 (about 90–98 in 100). The always-present group shows the mirror image: earlier about 13–26 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A34 and none were observed to A29; later about 16–25 in 100 go to A29 and none to A34. A33's outgoing transitions shifted from the always-present group (about 16–26 in 100 each) to the rarer group (about 16–21 in 100 each), and A44's shifted from the rarer group to the always-present group. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012]
- Close adjacencies moved with the blocks. Earlier, A19 was immediately followed by A29 (about 98 in 100 of 43 observations), A44 immediately preceded A19 (about 83 in 100 of 42), A33 was followed within five steps by each of A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 (about 193–199 traces each), and A24 reached A34 within five steps in about 194 traces. In the later window A33 immediately precedes A23 (about 95 in 100 of 41 observations), A23 immediately precedes A34 (about 98 in 100 of 42) and A20 precedes A29 within five steps in about 198 traces, while the earlier adjacencies shrink to 1–2 observations. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011]
- Participation itself barely moved: the rarer group stayed at about 17–24 in 100 traces in both windows and the always-present group at 100 in 100; A29 (in every trace) shifted only from mean relative position about 0.36 to about 0.48 and A33 from about 0.54 to about 0.66, remaining between the two groups in both windows. [POS001, POS005, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the two activity groups exchanged their place in the flow. In the earlier window A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 ran first and led to A29, while A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 ran after A29 and A33 and led to A34; in the later window A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 ran first and led to A29, A29 and A33 followed, and A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 ran last and led to A34, with A44 now feeding the always-present group and A33 preceding the rarer group. [REL011, REL012, REL022, REL030, DIR001, DIR002, DIR009, DIR011, DIR012, LAG002, LAG008]

The reordering is shown directly and consistently: within-trace order relations reverse in about 99 in 100 of the traces containing both activities for the pairs against A29 and A33, the positional shifts, successor changes and adjacency changes all point the same way, and the 73 qualifying control-flow items (against roughly 0.9 expected without change) cannot be explained by sampling. Every involved activity has substantial support in both windows, so the difference is not activities appearing or disappearing, and the reversal holds in essentially every shared trace rather than in a shifting minority of cases. [REL011, REL021, REL022, POS002, DIR004, LAG002, LAG005]

Limitations: the DIR, POS, REL and LAG items largely describe this one reordering from different angles and are not independent confirmations; several adjacency items rest on only 1–2 observations on one side; and the flow is characterised through pairwise relations with A29, A33, A44 and A34 rather than its complete wiring. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a wholesale switch between two fixed variants that differ in block order, which would look identical to a reordering of a single flow; the internal order within each group is also not characterised. [LAG001, LAG003, LAG008, LAG011, REL001]

Other differences: only peripheral, low-share transitions moved — for example A44→A06 fell from about 5 in 100 to about 2 in 100 of A44's observed outgoing transitions, and a few transitions of about 0.5–1 in 100 appear on one side only (such as A20→A05 or A25→A40) — and the rarer group's trace share fluctuated slightly within about 17–24 in 100; none of this alters the main picture. [DIR002, DIR007, DIR012, POS001, POS008, POS010]
